title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This integrated playbook centralizes Applied ML evaluation activities used across model onboarding, prompt set and benchmark creation, quantization profiling, and regression triage. It codifies standards for the eval-harness, ownership, SLOs, triage workflow, and the minimal artifacts required to move a model from prototype -> production in Redwood Inference.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers
- Model owners and research engineers
- Platform engineers (serving/runtime)
- Product managers responsible for LLM features

Goals:
- Ensure repeatable, measurable model onboarding with clear quality gates
- Minimize false positives/negatives from quantization and performance regressions
- Provide a single source of truth for prompt sets, metrics, and triage steps

Contents:
1) Eval Harness Standards
2) Model Onboarding Checklist
3) Prompt Sets and Benchmarking Guidelines
4) Quality Guardrails and Acceptance Criteria
5) Quantization Profile Process and Configs
6) Regression Triage Playbook
7) Ownership, SLAs, and Runbook Links

1) Eval Harness Standards
- Purpose: The eval harness is the canonical runner for deterministic, reproducible evaluation across models and workloads. All onboarding and regression tests must be runnable via the harness.
- Requirements:
  - Versioned harness image: ghcr.redwood-inference/internal/eval-harness:v{semver}
  - Deterministic seeds for generation tasks (seed logged per-run)
  - Standardized metric outputs: JSON lines with fields: run_id, model, task, prompt_set_id, metric_name, metric_value, confidence_interval
  - CI integration: every model PR must trigger harness smoke tests (fast subset) and nightly full-suite runs for models in the production catalog
- SLOs for the harness itself:
  - Test run reproducibility >= 99.9% (same inputs -> same outputs ordering and metrics within epsilon)
  - Job completion time for full suite on CI: target < 12 hours (parallelized)

2) Model Onboarding Checklist (minimum artifacts)
- Owner and contact: model_owner@redwood.com
- Artifacts required before 'canary' rollout:
  1. Model card (model-card.md) — architecture, pretraining corpus summary, license, known limitations
  2. Eval report (eval-report.jsonl) — harness-produced metrics across standard prompt sets and edge-case tests
  3. Latency/throughput profile — p95, p99 single-request latency on target infra, tokens/sec under batching scenarios
  4. Quantization profile (if applicable) — expected accuracy delta, supported quant modes
  5. Safety/guardrail checks — toxic/PII hit-rate < thresholds (see section 4)
  6. Rollout plan — canary %, rollback criteria, monitoring dashboards and alert contacts
- Onboarding Steps (numbered):
  1. Create candidate model branch and add model card and manifest to model-onboarding repo.
  2. Run unit harness smoke tests (fast set). If failures -> address and iterate.
  3. Run full eval-harness suite. Upload eval-report to central S3 and attach link to onboarding PR.
  4. If quantization is planned, run quantization profile job (see section 5) and verify quality gates.
  5. Submit canary rollout request in Redwood Console with specified metrics and thresholds.
  6. Monitor canary for 72 hours or until SLOs satisfied. Promote or rollback per plan.

3) Prompt Sets and Benchmarking Guidelines
- Prompt set taxonomy:
  - Core: high-coverage prompts representing main customer intents (maintained by product + applied-ml)
  - Edge: rare or adversarial inputs designed to elicit failure modes
  - Safety: toxicity, PII, safety-critical prompts
  - Regression: historical prompts that previously failed to catch regressions
- Naming convention: {domain}-{purpose}-{vYYYYMMDD}. Example: customer-support-core-v20260615
- Bench creation process:
  1. Curate candidate prompts (min 500 for core; 100-200 for edge/safety as appropriate)
  2. Annotate expected outputs or evaluation rubric (human or automated scoring)
  3. Run baseline model(s) to establish reference metrics and store as benchmark baseline
  4. Add to harness with metadata: prompt_set_id, domain, tags, owner
- Metrics to collect per prompt set: ROUGE/Exact Match/EM, BLEU (when applicable), factuality score (model-specific), safety hit-rate, response length, latency, and per-token cost estimate.

4) Quality Guardrails and Acceptance Criteria
- High-level guardrails:
  - Safety: toxic content generation rate must be <= 0.5% on safety prompt set for public-facing models; for sensitive customers the threshold is <= 0.1%
  - Factuality: for knowledge tasks, factuality delta vs baseline <= 3 percentage points (absolute)
  - Semantic quality: core prompt set weighted quality score >= baseline - 2 points
  - Latency: p95 single-request latency must meet target for the deployment tier (hosted: <= 220ms; dedicated: <= 180ms; internal staging: <= 300ms)
  - Token cost: per-token inference cost must not exceed budgeted cost for target tier; quantized variants must document expected savings
- Acceptance gates (automated):
  - All harness metrics present and in expected schema
  - No critical safety test failures
  - Latency and p95/p99 within thresholds
  - Regression delta on regression prompt set <= configured threshold (default 1.5%)

5) Quantization Profiles (process & example configs)
- Purpose: Provide reproducible experiments to measure accuracy/latency/cost tradeoffs for different quant modes (e.g., int8, int4, GPTQ-style).
- Required outputs:
  - quant-profile.csv (fields: model, quant_mode, accuracy_delta, latency_p95_ms, cost_delta_percent, notes)
  - quant-artifacts: quantized weights, quantization script/version, seed used for calibration
- Profile process:
  1. Start from exported FP16 model artifact with exact git hash recorded.
  2. Run calibration with 10k representative tokens (use same prompt sampling policy as production).
  3. Evaluate quantized model with full harness (core + safety + regression prompt sets).
  4. Record accuracy_delta = (metric_quant - metric_fp16) for each key metric.
  5. If accuracy_delta > allowed_delta (default 1.5% absolute for core metrics), mark profile as FAILED for production use.
- Example quant profile table:
| model        | quant_mode | accuracy_delta | latency_p95_ms | cost_delta_percent | notes            |
| redwood-7b   | int8       | 0.9%           | 140            | -45%               | acceptable       |
| redwood-7b   | int4-gptq  | 2.6%           | 95             | -62%               | quantify further |

- Recommended labels for quant profiles: "quant-supported", "quant-experimental"

6) Regression Triage Playbook
- Triggering events:
  - CI/regression suite failure on master or nightly job
  - Canary-alert from production (threshold breach)
  - Customer-reported quality degradation
- Triage owner: the model owner is the default triage lead; if absent, applied-ml-oncall takes ownership.
- Immediate steps (within 1 hour):
  1. Triage lead acknowledges and creates an incident ticket in JIRA (tag: regression-triage).
  2. Capture diffs: upload failing eval-run JSONL and compare to baseline run_id. Use harness comparator tool: bin/compare-evals --baseline <id> --current <id> --out diff-report.json
  3. Determine regression class: code/serving bug | model weight change | quantization issue | prompt change | new data distribution
- Diagnostic checklist (ordered):
  1. Re-run harness for current model commit and for the most recent known-good model commit to confirm delta.
  2. If quantized variant involved, re-run FP16 vs quantized to isolate quantization delta.
  3. Check recent infra/serving changes (kernel or runtime updates) that could affect numerical behavior.
  4. Inspect prompt set changes or scoring rubric modifications.
  5. Validate for data drift: sample production requests and compare distribution to training/benchmark prompts.
- Resolution paths:
  - Serving bug: revert or patch release with priority per severity.
  - Model regression due to weights: roll back to previous production model and schedule remediation with research.
  - Quantization failure: mark quant profile as FAILED and remove that variant from routing policies until fixed.
  - Prompt/regression from prompt set change: revert prompt set and re-run canonical evaluation.
- Post-incident:
  - Complete postmortem within 3 business days for production-impacting regressions.
  - Update regression prompt set with new failing examples if relevant.
  - Add a targeted unit test to harness to prevent reintroduction.

7) Ownership, SLAs and Runbook Links
- Owners and contacts:
  - Applied ML evaluations team (primary): applied-ml@redwood.com
  - Eval harness maintainer: eng-evals@redwood.com
  - Quantization tooling: eng-serving-runtime@redwood.com
  - Oncall: see eng-sre/oncall roster page
- SLAs and alerting:
  - Canary regression alert: P0 (15 minute response), escalate to oncall and product if not acknowledged
  - Nightly full-suite failure: P1 (4 hour response)
- Useful runbooks and pages (links):
  - /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
  - /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
  - /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/model-deploy-rollout-runbook

Appendices:
A) Example harness CLI commands:
- Run full suite locally: 
  bin/run-harness --config configs/full-suite.yaml --model-path /artifacts/redwood-7b/fp16 --out results/redwood-7b-full.jsonl
- Compare runs: 
  bin/compare-evals --baseline results/redwood-7b-baseline.jsonl --current results/redwood-7b-full.jsonl --out results/diff.json

B) Minimal eval-report JSONL schema (each line is a JSON object):
{
  "run_id": "20261015-redwood-7b",
  "model": "redwood-7b",
  "prompt_set_id": "customer-support-core-v20260615",
  "metrics": "{\"exact_match\":0.82,\"factuality\":0.91}",
  "latency_p95_ms": "142",
  "notes": "quant:int8"
}

C) Quick reference acceptance thresholds (defaults):
- Core quality delta <= 2.0% absolute
- Regression prompt set delta <= 1.5% absolute
- Safety hit-rate <= 0.5% (public)
- Latency p95 host <= 220ms
